papers.title_en: MemPlan: Memory-Conditioned PDDL Planning for Partially Observable Text Environments
papers.evidence: 面向LLM智能体的记忆条件规划，使用正负交互记忆
papers.tldr: LLM作为长程规划器成本高且易产生幻觉或无效动作。MemPlan将LLM约束为语言到符号规划的桥梁，在部分可观测文本环境中每步重建PDDL问题，并用正负图记忆引导假设检查与排除已证伪候选。在TextWorld、ALFWorld和Robotouille上，它提升任务完成率与步骤效率，并显著降低在线token开销。其贡献是记忆条件化符号规划与可复用的语言—符号接口。
papers.abstract_en: LLM agents are flexible in language interaction, but using them as long-horizon planners is costly and prone to hallucinated or invalid actions. This paper targets a different role for LLMs: constrained bridges between language and symbolic planning. We propose MemPlan, a memory-conditioned PDDL planning framework for partially observable interactive text environments. MemPlan keeps the PDDL domain fixed and reconstructs the PDDL problem at each step from parsed observations, candidate hypotheses, and interaction memory. Positive graph memory assigns relevance-based action costs to candidate hypotheses for missing objects, locations, or conditions, guiding the planner toward more plausible checks. Negative memory records execution-refuted assumptions and compiles them into exclusion constraints, preventing repeated attempts at candidates already contradicted by feedback. A unified schema-conditioned language--symbol interface, trained offline with supervised fine-tuning, connects text environments to the planning loop through observation-to-fact parsing and symbolic-action-to-command grounding. Experiments on TextWorld, ALFWorld, and Robotouille show that MemPlan improves task completion and step efficiency over language-only and PDDL-aware baselines, while substantially reducing online token cost compared with LLM-planning baselines such as ReAct. The same fine-tuned interface is also reused across TextWorld task types without task-specific fine-tuning. Our code and data are available at: https://github.com/tewiSong/MemPlan.

papers.title_en: Governance-State Corruption in Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents: A Cross-Model Stress Test
papers.authors: Bowen Liu, Youting Wang, Bonan Shen, Dingyan Shang
papers.evidence: 长期记忆检索中的治理状态损坏
papers.tldr: LLM智能体可能检索到正确记忆，却在有效性状态变化后误用。本文提出“治理状态损坏”，在六家提供商、731个基准基座和2080对匹配故障上做跨模型压力测试。离线检查中96.25%的损坏改变有效投影，oracle执行可100%恢复；下游LongMemEval/Memora面板显示清洁与损坏正确率差达40.54和30.60个百分点。结果表明应把记忆控制状态完整性纳入评测，而不仅看检索准确率。
papers.abstract_en: An LLM agent can retrieve a memory correctly yet use it incorrectly after its validity state changes. We study governance-state corruption: faults that alter which retained records enter model-visible context while stored content and tasks remain fixed. Across six providers, 731 benchmark-grounded bases yield 2,080 matched fault pairs. In offline control-plane checks, corruption changes the operative projection in 96.25% of pairs, while oracle-backed enforcement restores it in 100%. For downstream evaluation, a deterministically selected, non-probability LongMemEval/Memora panel resolves 298 of 300 matched triplets (238 distinct bases). Clean-minus-corrupted contrasts are 40.54 percentage points in LongMemEval binary correctness (95% base-cluster interval [30.32, 50.71]) and 30.60 points in rescaled Memora FAMA ([23.31, 37.69]); both sources also show recovery. OAKS Novel native option parity holds for all 6,714 resolved outputs. Full-cohort frozen-scorer corruption/recovery effects (-27.55/+27.51 points) remain descriptive proxies, not validated native semantic population effects. These bounded findings motivate evaluating memory control-state integrity alongside retrieval accuracy.

papers.title_en: Your Home Remembers: A Voice-Enabled Household Memory Assistant for Conversational Retrieval
papers.authors: Aleix Sant, Jordi Luque, Fernando López, Pablo Gómez, Carlos Escolano
papers.evidence: 存储与检索家庭对话的会话记忆助手
papers.tldr: 家庭日常信息多散落在对话中，容易被遗忘或记错。论文提出一款语音智能家居助手，在 Android 平板上以模块化编排层集成语音识别、说话人分离、嵌入与语言模型，通过唤醒词和 VAD 实现免手持查询。系统将录音分块转写、分离说话人并构建带时间戳的轮次段落，存入向量库，再用检索增强生成回答记忆查询。界面支持录音、对话管理和来源核查，展示了可配置的家庭记忆检索原型。
papers.abstract_en: Everyday household information is often exchanged in conversations but never written down, making details easy to forget or misremember. We present a voice-enabled smart-home assistant that acts as a household memory by recording conversations and retrieving information from stored and newly captured speech. The assistant runs on an Android tablet with a modular architecture in which speech-recognition, diarisation, embedding and language models can be configured or replaced through an orchestration layer. On-device wake-word detection and VAD-based query capture support hands-free interaction. Recorded audio is processed in configurable chunks, transcribed and diarised, converted into turn-aware passages with conversation-level timestamps, and indexed in a vector store. For memory queries, a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline selects key passages and uses them to generate an answer. The interface supports recording, conversation management and inspection of timestamped sources.

papers.title_en: Muffin - A Shared Memory Buffer for Asynchronous AI Agents
papers.authors: Ping-Lin Kuo, Suman Navaratnarajah, Christian Frey, Gresa Shala, Josif Grabocka
papers.evidence: 面向异步多智能体系统的共享记忆缓冲协议
papers.tldr: 面向目标驱动的多智能体推理常因交互中关键信息交换不畅而失败，现有辩论范式又依赖同步轮流发言与全轨迹共享。MUFFIN 采用异步智能体框架：编排器按推理需求路由查询，将高难度任务交给多智能体，并用共享内存缓冲区异步交换中间发现，同时保留个体私有推理。在20项基准中17项取得最高准确率，相较多智能体辩论提升19.2个准确率点并减少77.4% token，且无需共享完整轨迹。其贡献在于以更优质量-成本权衡改善智能体协作的信息协调。
papers.abstract_en: The rise of Agentic AI systems has changed the landscape of artificial intelligence by enabling strong reasoning capabilities through specialized multi-agent interaction with structured self-reflection. However, in target-driven reasoning tasks, single- and multi-agent systems are often on par in terms of performance gains. A major challenge is that failures often arise from an ineffective exchange of critical information during inter-agent interaction and coordination. Different from existing multi-agent debate paradigms that rely on synchronous turn-taking and sharing information across different agents, we propose an inter-agent protocol based on shared Memory bUFFer INference - referred to as MUFFIN - in an asynchronous agentic framework. In the first step, an orchestrator routes queries based on their reasoning demands and delegates demanding ones to a multi-agent setting, where a shared memory buffer provides asynchronous exchange of intermediate findings while an agent's private reasoning remains local. Our experiments show that our framework Muffin outperforms established competitors, achieving the best accuracy in 17 out of 20 of our benchmark settings, and provides a better quality-cost trade-off than multi-agent debate: Muffin improves accuracy by 19.2 accuracy points while using 77.4% fewer tokens, without requiring full-trace sharing.

papers.title_en: Hypergraph-Enhanced Evidence Selection for Long-Context Multimodal Document QA
papers.authors: Wenxin Zhao, Jiachuan Wang, Xinyi Zhu, Jiake Ge, Haoyang Li, Yongqi Zhang, Shuangyin Li, Lei Chen
papers.evidence: 面向长上下文多模态文档RAG的预算感知超图证据选择
papers.tldr: 长上下文多模态文档问答需在有限输入预算下跨页跨模态定位证据，现有RAG依赖页或块等固定粒度静态规则，易造成信息损失。本文提出HyperDoc，将核心任务形式化为预算感知的结构化证据选择，并构建文档超图显式建模结构、逻辑与跨模态关系。在超图上按查询意图和输入预算自适应选择代价感知超边，形成紧凑而充分的证据。三个基准实验表明其优于多类SOTA基线，为长文档多模态RAG提供新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Long-context multimodal document question answering (QA) has become an important yet challenging task for modern vision-language models (VLMs), as it requires reasoning over evidence dispersed across pages and modalities within limited input budgets. Current pipelines adopt retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to select multimodal evidence for downstream VLMs. However, existing systems mainly rely on static selection rules over fixed-granularity retrieval units such as pages or blocks, resulting in information loss during retrieval and suboptimal performance in downstream reasoning. To alleviate these issues, we formulate the core task as budget-aware evidence selection over structured document evidence and propose HyperDoc, a document RAG framework that constructs compact yet sufficient evidence while preserving document relations. Specifically, HyperDoc constructs a document hypergraph to explicitly capture structural, logical, and cross-modal relationships among multimodal document elements. Over this structured evidence space, HyperDoc performs adaptive cost-aware hyperedge selection based on query intent and input budget. Extensive experiments on three representative benchmarks demonstrate that HyperDoc outperforms various types of state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title_en: RouteDRAG: Learning to Route and Control Agentic Execution for Multimodal Document RAG
papers.authors: Zekai Chen, Hao Zhu, Yu Liu, Xunkai Li, Zejian Kang, Rui Qian, Quanjiang Li, Rong-Hua Li
papers.evidence: 学习路由与控制多模态文档的智能体式检索增强生成
papers.tldr: 多模态文档问答常需跨页、表格与图整合信息，但Agentic RAG并非总有必要，额外检索可能增加计算并损害准确率。RouteDRAG以图结构统一索引组织多模态内容，并用自适应路径路由判断是否调用Agent，再以动态执行和顺序策略学习控制工具使用与终止。在两个基准上，它仅将79.3%查询交给Agent，却比仅短路径执行平均提升3.47个百分点，并超过统一Agent执行且回答调用更少。该工作表明按查询收益路由并控制Agent执行，可在多模态文档RAG中兼顾准确率与效率。
papers.abstract_en: Web-based applications increasingly rely on understanding long multimodal documents, where answering questions often requires combining information across pages, tables, and figures. Agentic retrieval-augmented generation addresses these tasks through iterative retrieval and reasoning. However, Agentic execution is not always necessary, introducing additional computation and potentially incorrect answers. Our empirical analysis reveals that Agentic execution provides query-dependent benefits, while additional operations may improve, preserve, or degrade answer accuracy. These findings motivate controlling both Agent invocation and subsequent execution. To address these challenges, we propose RouteDRAG, a learning-based framework comprising four components. Unified Document Index organizes multimodal content into a graph-backed index and derives query representations from initial retrieval. Adaptive Path Routing preserves exact answering and predicts the relative benefit of Agent over shorter execution paths. Dynamic Agent Execution maintains an evolving workspace and refines Planner proposals to control tool use and termination. Sequential Policy Learning first trains operation control from observed outcomes and then trains path routing using the resulting Agent's performance. Across two benchmarks, RouteDRAG achieves an average accuracy improvement of 3.47 percentage points over shorter-path-only execution while assigning only 79.3% of queries to Agent. Notably, it also surpasses uniform Agent execution on both benchmarks while requiring fewer answering calls. Our code is now available at https://github.com/Ereshkigal1/RouteDRAG.

papers.title_en: DuQUAD: A Dual-View Framework with Quality-Aware Evidence Pruning for Multi-Document Question Answering
papers.authors: Yeonjun Choi, Seyeon Jeong, Jong Wook Kim, Beakcheol Jang
papers.evidence: 提出面向多文档问答的RAG框架，采用双视角推理与质量感知证据剪枝
papers.tldr: 多文档检索增强问答中，大模型常忽略上下文中部证据，形成“Lost in the Middle”问题。DuQUAD通过结构融合分数引导的局部代理与全局代理进行双视图推理，缓解位置偏置，并用质量评分和句级剪枝过滤噪声证据。实验显示，其平均准确率较最强基线提升3.0%，金证据召回率提升9.4%，并显著降低多代理框架的计算开销。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models with retrieval-augmented generation systematically underutilize evidence in the middle of multi-document contexts, a phenomenon known as Lost in the Middle. Existing mitigation strategies, such as document reordering and attention steering, can reduce boundary bias but remain brittle in noisy settings, where inaccurate relevance estimation and spurious documents still obscure useful evidence in central positions. We propose DuQUAD, a multi-document QA framework that mitigates positional bias through dual-view reasoning and quality-aware evidence pruning. DuQUAD combines a Local Agent guided by a Structural Fusion Score with a Global Agent that reasons over the full document set, providing both targeted evidence recovery and broad contextual understanding. The framework further filters candidate evidence using explicit quality scoring and refines it at the sentence level to reduce noise. DuQUAD consistently outperforms strong Lost-in-the-Middle mitigation baselines, including hybrid retrieval and reranking, multi-agent reasoning, and context optimization methods, improving accuracy by 3.0% on average over the strongest competing baseline and gold evidence recall by 9.4%, while substantially reducing computational cost compared to existing multi-agent frameworks.

papers.title_en: CoLink: Global Compression and Knowledge Linking for Multi-Turn Dialogue Modeling
papers.authors: Lian Yan, Zhenbo Xia, Haotian Wang, Chen Tang, Yi Guan, Jie Liu, Jingchi Jiang
papers.evidence: 面向多轮对话的历史压缩与记忆关联
papers.tldr: 长程多轮对话中，LLM受限于上下文窗口，难以从冗余历史中提取关键信息；现有组织或局部优化方法易致信息损失与检索冗余。CoLink将历史聚类为主题图并与外部知识建立跨语义关联，结合语义相关性与图拓扑检索激活知识。它基于信息理论推导核心语义压缩目标，并用竞争槽机制将全局上下文凝缩为紧凑记忆与知识槽。在公开数据集和MMD上，CoLink在知识链接与语义建模上表现更优，验证了其有效性与泛化性。
papers.abstract_en: Extracting salient information from long-horizon dialogue histories remains a significant challenge for Large Language Models (LLMs) due to the restricted context windows and efficient retrieval challenges. Current methods typically rely on history organization or local token-level optimization, suffering from information loss, retrieval redundancy, and myopic attention. Inspired by the view in cognitive science that dialogue constitutes sense-making and memory association, we propose CoLink, a framework that enhances LLMs' global context awareness in domain-specific multi-turn dialogues through information linking and compression. CoLink first clusters historical contexts into topic graphs to establish cross-semantic associations with external knowledge. Guided by the adaptive control of thought, it then retrieves and activates knowledge via synergizing semantic relevance and graph-structural topology. Crucially, to achieve effective compression of history and knowledge, we ground multi-turn dialogues in information theory and derive a principled optimization objective for extracting the core sense-making information. Coupled with a competitive slot mechanism, CoLink condenses the global context into dedicated memory and knowledge slots, efficiently distilling lengthy, redundant inputs into an extremely compact latent representation. Extensive empirical results on both public and our MMD datasets validate CoLink's superiority and generalizability in knowledge linking and sense modeling.

papers.title_en: The Right Fact, the Wrong Decision: SciValidityBench for Scientific Agent Memory
papers.evidence: 提出SciValidityBench，评估科学智能体召回的长时记忆是否可用于决策
papers.tldr: 现有智能体记忆评测多聚焦检索，但科学智能体还须判断记住的事实是否在特定科学状态下可用于决策。作者提出 SciValidityBench，以64个TaskSpecs覆盖五类有效性模块和六个领域，并用SciStateForge把历史编译为决策治理状态。四类模型上，编译状态较通用事件图提升9.2–18.8个百分点。该工作将记忆评测从找对事实推进到判断事实能否支配决策。
papers.abstract_en: Most agent-memory benchmarks frame long-term memory as retrieval: can an agent recover the relevant record from a long and evolving history? Scientific agents face a stricter problem: a correctly remembered fact may still be invalid to use. The same reported test result can support confirmation when the outcome and stopping rule were fixed in advance, yet only exploration when the outcome was selected from twenty inspected results. We call this scientific use validity: whether remembered evidence is eligible to influence a decision under the state governing its interpretation. We introduce SciValidityBench, an executable benchmark factory with 64 TaskSpecs spanning five validity modules and six scientific domains. TaskSpecs couple generated experimental histories with scientific-state definitions, programmatic decision oracles, controlled interventions, and automatic scoring. The SciStateForge compiler-reader framework turns distributed histories into explicit decision-governing state. Counterfactual pairs and targeted corruption-repair controls then test whether models use those dependencies and localize failures. Across four model families, compiled scientific state improves valid decision-making by 9.2-18.8 percentage points over a generic Event Graph. Retrieval alone does not reproduce this cross-family gain, while content-identical flat and typed views show that the improvement comes from exposing governing state rather than a particular graph serialization. SciValidityBench thus shifts memory evaluation from finding the right fact to deciding whether that fact should control the decision.

papers.title_en: MemVLN: Streaming Episodic Memory for Vision-Language Navigation
papers.authors: Yan Wang, Jiangyong Huang, Siyuan Huang, Baoxiong Jia
papers.evidence: 面向具身视觉语言导航智能体的流式情景记忆框架
papers.tldr: 视觉语言导航在长时程任务中难以维持持续情节记忆，基于VLM的流式智能体尤其受限。MemVLN构建带时间步与动作相对位姿的有界压缩感知特征库，经交叉注意力生成紧凑记忆token，并配合冻结几何编码器。方法用掩码轨迹摘要与多粒度子轨迹分解训练记忆模块，仅凭情节记忆重建路线。在R2R/RxR导航训练下，其在VLN-CE多数指标达SOTA；真实场景留出回合成功率由17%升至40%，后训练达47%。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to follow language instructions through 3D environments. Maintaining persistent episodic memory remains a challenge for VLM-based streaming agents in long-horizon navigation. We present MEMVLN, a streaming episodic memory framework that maintains a bounded bank of compressed perceptual features annotated with timesteps and action-derived relative poses, and produces compact memory tokens via cross-attention. We pair the proposed memory with a frozen pretrained geometry encoder. To learn the memory module, we design a masking-based trajectory summarization task with multi-granularity sub-trajectory decomposition, encouraging route reconstruction exclusively from episodic memory. Under navigation training restricted to the official R2R/RxR trajectories, MEMVLN achieves state-of-the-art performance on most reported metrics on standard VLN-CE benchmarks. Long-horizon analyses further characterize when episodic memory is useful. For physical evaluation, we collect 30 instruction-conditioned episodes in one physical scene, use 24 as demonstrations for post-training, and hold out six for testing. On the held-out episodes, MEMVLN improves success over the VLM baseline from 17% to 40%, and post-training further raises it to 47%.

papers.title_en: RetroNav: Scene-Grounded Retrospection and Retry for Self-Evolving Lifelong Navigation
papers.authors: Diantao Tu, Yangdong Liu, Niannian Dai, Mengqi Rong, Shuhan Shen
papers.evidence: 积累导航经验的统一记忆系统
papers.tldr: 现有机器人导航多聚焦孤立任务，难以在重复导航中积累经验并反思失败。RetroNav是免训练的自进化导航框架，用统一记忆系统连接场景几何语义知识与历史导航经验，并区分客观观察和任务解释。每次尝试后由独立评估器判断是否重试，需要时反思智能体依据场景证据复盘历史决策，生成重试简报指导下一轮。该方法在五个导航基准取得最优性能，为终身导航提供可反思、可重试的新范式。
papers.abstract_en: Existing robot navigation methods primarily focus on isolated tasks, overlooking the need to accumulate knowledge and experience across repeated navigation episodes. Although recent lifelong navigation methods have explored cross-task knowledge accumulation, they mainly focus on scene knowledge while neglecting historical navigation experience and its connection to scene evidence, limiting the ability to reflect on past mistakes and improve future decisions. To address this limitation, this paper presents RetroNav, a training-free self-evolving navigation framework that integrates navigation, memory accumulation, and failure reflection. Specifically, we develop a unified memory system that connects geometric and semantic scene knowledge with historical navigation experience, distinguishing objective observations from task-dependent interpretations. After each navigation attempt, an independent evaluator determines whether a retry is necessary. If so, a Retrospection Agent revisits historical decisions using accumulated scene knowledge and navigation records, generating an evidence-grounded retry brief to guide the next attempt. RetroNav achieves state-of-the-art performance across five navigation benchmarks. Our method will be open-sourced at https://github.com/3dv-casia/RetroNav .

papers.title_en: Self-Keyed In-Parameter Memorization for External Memory-Free Dialogue Recall in Frozen Language Models
papers.authors: XinYu Piao, Myunghoon Ryu, Joongheon Kim, Jong-Kook Kim
papers.evidence: 无需外部存储的参数内对话记忆
papers.tldr: 大模型通常依赖随对话增长的外部存储，本文研究无外部记忆且不知未来问题的设定下，能否把对话写入模型参数并在之后召回。提出SKIM，让模型为每轮对话自生成多样化问题，以这些问题作为参数中的键写入，用户提问时从参数中检索并回答。在五个语言模型上，SKIM能从后续问题召回多数已存对话轮次，且无需外部存储。该工作验证了参数内记忆用于对话召回的可能性。
papers.abstract_en: A large language model maintains conversational content in an external storage that is outside the model and grows as the dialogue continues. This work assumes an environment where a language model has no external memory and no prior knowledge of the future question or its answer. The motivation is to research whether a dialogue can be stored in the model parameters and later answer a question about it. This work proposes self-keyed in-parameter memorization (SKIM), a closed-form method in which the model generates its own questions about each dialogue turn and writes those questions into its parameters as the keys that later retrieve the turn's content. Generating many varied questions for each turn allows a later user question to match one even when phrased differently, and its answer is recalled from the parameters alone. Evaluated on five language models, SKIM recalls most stored dialogue turns from later user questions, and it answers from the model parameters without any external storage.

papers.title_en: From Interaction to Capability: Task Advancement as State and Supervision for GUI Agents
papers.authors: Ziyang Chen, Qian Li, Chengwei Qin
papers.evidence: 任务进展记忆保存已验证的任务进展并为智能体学习可复用操作
papers.tldr: 长程GUI任务中，跨应用信息与失败尝试交织，使记忆难以保留有效进展并沉淀可复用操作。TAM将任务推进定义为经核验的任务进度，用推进状态更新剩余目标，并在任务后监督抽取产生局部验证结果的交互。MobileWorld上仅推进状态将成功率从12.0%提升至28.2%，完整TAM相对最强基线提升17.6%，每解决任务token降38.7%。该工作把交互经验转化为可复用能力，提升长程GUI智能体的执行效率与成功率。
papers.abstract_en: GUI memory should preserve the results of past actions and learn reusable operations. This is difficult in long-horizon workflows, where agents must use information across applications and useful operations are interleaved with failed attempts. We introduce Task Advancement Memory (TAM), which defines task advancement as verified task progress, and supports ongoing task execution and learns reusable operations. During execution, Task Advancement State represents how verified task progress changes the remaining goals, allowing the agent to build on earlier achievements across applications. After each task, advancement supervision identifies and abstracts the interactions that produced a verified local result. The learned operations preserve the relation between required inputs, expected outcomes, and verification conditions. This retains locally successful operations from both successful and failed tasks. On MobileWorld GUI-only tasks, Advancement State alone raises success from 12.0% to 28.2%. Full TAM achieves a 17.6% relative gain in task success over the strongest evaluated baseline and reduces lifecycle tokens per solved task by 38.7%. On SPA-Bench, TAM achieves state-of-the-art task success in the single-app English Level 3 setting.

papers.title_en: SkillMem: Compact External Skill Memory for Latent Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.authors: Yuxuan Zhu, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Pin-Yu Chen, Keerthiram Murugesan
papers.evidence: 可直接供智能体使用的外部潜在技能记忆
papers.tldr: 潜在多智能体系统通过将推理与通信保持在连续表示中来降低推理成本，但可复用技能通常以文本、逐层KV或技能专属参数存储，导致重复处理或存储开销大。SkillMem将每个技能表示为小型外部潜在记忆，并用角色条件交叉注意力读取器在潜在推理中直接调用。通过行为蒸馏训练记忆与读取器且冻结主干，在六个基准和Qwen3 4B至14B上取得稳定增益。百技能库存储降低逾38倍，端到端推理最高加速4.23倍。
papers.abstract_en: Latent multi-agent systems reduce inference cost by keeping intermediate reasoning and inter-agent communication in continuous representations.\ Reusable skills, however, are commonly supplied as text or stored as layer-wise Key-Value states or skill-specific model parameters, introducing repeated processing or substantial per-skill storage.\ We introduce \textbf{SkillMem}, which represents each reusable skill as a small external latent memory and makes it directly available during latent multi-agent reasoning.\ A role-conditioned cross-attention reader allows the same memory to guide different agents according to their roles and current hidden states.\ We train the skill memories and shared reader through behavioral distillation, matching the change in token predictions induced by a textual skill while keeping the backbone frozen.\ For our experiments, we obtain textual skills from paired successful and failed multi-agent trajectories, although existing skills can also be compiled directly.\ Across six benchmarks and Qwen3 models ranging from 4B to 14B parameters, SkillMem provides strong gains for smaller backbones while preserving efficient latent multi-agent inference across model scales.\ We use the same $8\times256$ memory configuration across all evaluated model scales, requiring 9.6\,KB of skill-specific storage per skill, including its retrieval embedding.\ For a library of 100 skills, SkillMem reduces total storage by more than $38\times$ compared with alternative skill representations and achieves up to a $4.23\times$ end-to-end inference speedup.\ These results show that compact procedural memories can be reused without sacrificing the efficiency of latent multi-agent reasoning.

papers.authors: Michael Philip, Mahesh Balakrishnan, David Geraghty, David Mao, Vidhya Venkat, Ilya Mironov
papers.evidence: 将智能体历史轨迹路由到多种记忆系统进行保留
papers.tldr: 持续学习智能体常反复遇到相关问题，但单一记忆机制难适配多场景：全局历史成本高且混杂，固定压缩又丢失细节。Routed CL 将轨迹聚类，每簇从记忆库选一种系统保存状态，并用 LLM 路由器在运行前复用或新建簇，Context Memory Adapter 衔接记忆与智能体循环。在 CL-Bench 与 τ^3-Bench 混合流上，它较全局 ICL 提升归一化奖励达可获上限的 15-30%，并降低 65-72% API 成本。该工作把持续学习建模为同时选择学习机制与状态簇的路由问题。
papers.abstract_en: Agents deployed at scale repeatedly encounter related problems, and it is natural to let them learn from each other's experience rather than starting over each time. Unfortunately, there is no single way to retain that experience that works well across settings, and no way to know in advance which future problems a given experience will help with. A global history preserves every detail but becomes expensive and mixes together experience that may not belong together; compressing that history into one fixed representation limits the cost but can throw away valuable details.   We introduce Routed Continual Learning (Routed CL), an architecture that decides how to partition and retain experience. Past trajectories are grouped into clusters, each of which maintains state using one memory system from a fixed library. Before each run, an LLM-based router either reuses an existing cluster or creates a new one, basing its decision on the problem statement, memory system descriptions, and cluster summaries. We also introduce Context Memory Adapter, which mediates between the memory system and the agentic loop.   We evaluate the architecture on a heterogeneous stream that interleaves 301 instances from the six CL-Bench tasks with 97 banking instances from $τ^3$-Bench. Across four language models and five matched rollouts, Routed Continual Learning raises normalized reward over a single global in-context learning (ICL) history by 15-30% of the maximum attainable normalized reward, achieves higher mean normalized reward than ICL-only clustering, and reduces estimated API cost by 65-72% relative to Global ICL. These results support approaching continual learning as a routing problem that chooses both a learning mechanism and a state cluster rather than committing to one representation globally.

papers.title_en: Ask to Evolve: A Unified Harness for Lifelong Embodied Navigation with Hybrid Action Space and Persistent Memory
papers.authors: Kai Sheng, Liuyi Wang, Jinlong Li, Haojie Dai, Chengju Liu, Qijun Chen
papers.evidence: 具备持久记忆、可在终身任务间积累经验的具身智能体
papers.tldr: 具身导航智能体需同时解决如何移动、何时求助与经验复用问题。EvoLife统一框架融合路径点、局部离散、像素及物体导向的混合动作空间，支持主动交互与持久空间记忆。在八项基准、四类任务上，每回合平均仅1.87次主动交互，四组百回合首访成功率均达100%，LHPR-VLN与GOAT-Bench完整序列成功率分别达98%和94%。R2R重访SPL由82.23%升至93.31%，并在多日实体导航中展示探索、主动求助与记忆重访能力。
papers.abstract_en: Giving embodied agents the freedom to act autonomously, initiate interactions, and understand their surroundings through experience is a step toward bringing them to life in the physical world. Realizing this vision requires action, interaction, and memory to work together, so that each encounter can inform current decisions and contribute experience for future tasks. We present EvoLife, a unified navigation harness that enables a multimodal embodied agent to choose how to move, when to ask, and what experience to carry forward. Its hybrid action space supports waypoint navigation, local discrete adjustments, pixel-based navigation, and object-directed navigation. Active interaction allows the agent to seek clarification or assistance when it encounters ambiguity or difficulty, while persistent spatial memory binds observations and dialogue to places, retaining useful experience to guide subsequent visits. We evaluate eight benchmarks across four task families: vision-language navigation, object navigation, interactive instance navigation, and continuous multi-task navigation. With an average of only 1.87 active interactions per episode, our method achieves a first-visit success rate (SR) of 100% across four 100-episode sets spanning vision-language navigation and object navigation. Complete-sequence SR reaches 98% on 50 LHPR-VLN sequences and 94% on 50 GOAT-Bench sequences. In the R2R revisit setting, success weighted by path length (SPL) increases from 82.23% to 93.31% with retained experience. Multi-day physical navigation further demonstrates exploration, proactive help-seeking, and revisiting remembered places. Together, these results advance the vision of bringing embodied agents to life through autonomous action, proactive interaction, and the accumulation and reuse of experience.
